The given cation is the iminium salt that results from condensation of 2-pentanone with the tertiary amine N,N-dimethylethanamine.  
1. Treatment with the strong, non-nucleophilic base LDA in the ether solvent DME removes the acidic α-proton on carbon-3 of the iminium ion, giving the corresponding aza-enolate (the metallo-enamine).  
2. Alkylation with ethyl iodide then introduces an ethyl group at that α-carbon.  
3. Acidic hydrolysis of the resulting iminium regenerates the carbonyl compound and releases the free tertiary amine.

Starting from pentan-2-ylidene, installing an ethyl group at C-3 yields a seven-carbon ketone whose carbonyl is now at C-4:

CH3–CH2–CH2–CO–CH2–CH3  = heptan-4-one

The amine released is N,N-dimethylethanamine.

Thus:

Reagents (A):  
(i) LDA, DME (ii) CH3CH2I (iii) H3O+

Product (B): heptan-4-one + N,N-dimethylethanamine

Answer: C
